title: The month-bucketing defect: Script 01's day<=15 rule written as MonthBegin, which is a no-op for days 2-15

note: Found 2026-09-16 while building phase 27. `d - pd.offsets.MonthBegin(1)` rolls back only to the CURRENT month's first day, so the day<=15 branch does nothing for days 2-15. Sized: 49 of the 110 Sentinel scenes carry the wrong month; the floor-only rank correlation with the wells moves from +0.711 (as quoted in D-170) to +0.707 on corrected bucketing, with n rising 36 -> 44, so D-170's finding stands and its figure is inside the 0.01 churn threshold. _merge_calibration is LATENT only: the single calibration date is 2026-03-30, day 30. Phase 27 does not depend on any of it - it re-derives the month from each scene date and recomputes the wells' bar from the level frame. Whether the fix is three edits or one shared bucketing helper is Martin's call; regenerating the Sentinel CSV needs the publishing machine (T-31). The rule now has ONE implementation, utils.buckets.month_bucket, imported by 01_data_prep (both sites), comment_states, warren_flood_prep (4 sites) and sentinel_wet_floor (2 sites), and re-exported by model_utils. tools/month_bucket_lint.py is a new check_all gate: it proves the helper identical to all FIVE correct variants the tree carried over every date from 1990 to 2040 - exhaustive, because dates are the whole input domain - and fails if any live line buckets with MonthBegin again. title: 03_regional_averages.csv silently drops any month with no dipwell reading, and the climate goes with it
implements: D-166; RB-22; found by phase 27's missing-month guard
note: Found 2026-09-16 by phase 27, whose guard refuses to iterate a month with no P or PET rather than raising or inventing one. The file has 250 rows where its own span (2005-03 to 2026-02) needs 252: 2005-06 and 2022-12 are ABSENT. Both are present in the raw RAF_Valley_Climate.csv (2005-06 rain 18.8 mm, 2022-12 rain 91.8 mm) and in outputs/01_climate.csv, so nothing is lost upstream. They disappear in 03_state_space_model.py export_regional_averages(), which builds the frame from the cluster CENTROIDS and then `.join(climate[['P_m','PET']])` - a left join on the well index. Neither month has a single dipwell reading, so its climate is dropped with it. THE POINT: this file is a well-indexed frame that carries climate as passengers, not a climate record, and _pflood_climate() (phase 18, and phase 27 after it) reads it as one. Consequence in phase 27: the winter of 2022-23 is modelled with no December rainfall, in a December that had 91.8 mm. Two candidate fixes, both changing committed numbers and therefore Martin's call: read the climate from 01_climate.csv, which is complete, or make that join outer so the climate months survive without wells. Nothing was changed. FIXED 2026-09-16 (Martin: "Both"; D-171). export_regional_averages joins OUTER (Script 03 1.14.0), and _pflood_climate reads INT_CLIMATE with the climatology clipped to the well record's span - 01_climate.csv starts in 1930 and averaging it whole would have widened the climatology from 21 years to 96. Verified before acceptance: the two sources agree to 2.8e-14 mm on all 250 shared months, and only June and December climatology move (P -1.718 / -0.715 mm, PET -0.267 mm in December). OWED: a full pipeline run on the L14, after which this check goes green - and the published numbers of Scripts 14, 16, 17 and 28 move, so cite_check and audit_number_drift must be read and the corpus brought up to the new values. That corpus pass is NOT done.

title: The early record is sampled sub-monthly, so 2005-2006 monthly values are means of up to 5 visits while later ones are single readings - and 2005-06's data sits in May
implements: D-171; the measurement protocol in the project instructions; found answering Martin 2026-09-16
note: OPEN AS A RULING, not as work: the check only asserts the findings note exists, so the row surfaces until Martin decides. Measured from the raw sheet: 2022-12 is a GENUINE break (30/11/2022 to 01/02/2023, 63 days, no visit in the month), but 2005-06 is NOT - the wells were read on 07/06 and 14/06/2005 and BOTH bucket to May under the day<=15 rule, so June has no bucket while its data sits in May. Separately, 2005-2006 was sampled fortnightly or better (33 visits in 2006, up to 5 in one month) against 11-13 visits a year from 2007; 13 bucketed months average 2-5 visits and all 13 are in 2005-2006. So the monthly series changes definition at the 2006/2007 boundary: a mean over ~6 weeks early, a single end-of-month reading later. Not shown to affect any published number - no refit was run. Candidate tests are listed in the findings note. Decisions owed: whether the early sampling needs a stated treatment, and whether 2005-06 should be recovered from May. CORRECTED the same day, after Martin said these were not the breaks: they are NOT. The breaks are 2011-09 and 2017-01, where the raw sheet's dated column EXISTS and is EMPTY (0 wells in the 01/10/2011 and 01/02/2017 rounds) and Script 01 INTERPOLATED the whole network - 54 of 72 and 74 of 77 wells, against 1-4 everywhere else. They are invisible to a search for empty months (they were filled) and to a visit-interval test (the columns are regularly spaced; only their contents are missing). 2022-12 is a missed visit left empty; 2005-06 is a bucketing artefact with its data in May. The sub-monthly early-sampling finding stands. See the appended CORRECTION in the findings note.

title: The two recording breaks (2011-09, 2017-01) are interpolated network-wide, enter the fitted frame unfiltered, and are not disclosed in the Methods Supplement
implements: T-34; D-171; found 2026-09-16 at Martin's prompting
check: python3 -c "import pandas as pd;s=pd.read_csv('outputs/01_observation_states.csv');s=s.rename(columns={s.columns[0]:'m'});print(int(max((s[s['m'].astype(str).str.startswith(t)].drop(columns=['m']).eq('interpolated').sum(axis=1).sum()) for t in ('2011-09','2017-01'))))"
note: A RULING is owed, not work; the check pins the count so a silent change to the interpolation would surface. Measured: of the wells flagged interpolated in those months, 53/54 (2011-09) and 73/74 (2017-01) carry a value in 01_wells_all.csv, and 52/54 and 74/74 in 01_wells_clean.csv - the frame the SSM fits. Nothing in the fitting path filters on the flag (10j says so explicitly for its own use). ~127 well-months enter the fits as observations while being interpolations: ~0.6 % of the record but concentrated in two months, and 2017-01 is a WINTER month, where the winter maxima and recharge signal live. The flag exists and is correct - the question is whether the fits, the event detection and the documents should treat those months differently. Candidate checks in the findings note; none run. Nothing changed. DISCLOSURE CHECKED 2026-09-16 at Martin's request. The Supplement discloses the POLICY in full: S.1 gives clean_well_series limit=1 with the limit=3 rejection argued at length, the provenance file and its totals (14,747 measured / 275 interpolated / 4,478 missing), and S.3 states explicitly that the canonical fit runs exclude_interpolated=False so interpolated rows enter the design matrix, with exclude_interpolated=True as 'the documented sensitivity' that 'the chapter does not run'. So the mechanism is disclosed and my earlier concern about it being hidden is withdrawn. WHAT IS NOT DISCLOSED is these two months: 127 of the 275 interpolated cells (46.2 %) are 2017-01 (74) and 2011-09 (53), whole-network outages, while the other 248 months hold 148 at a median of 1. Neither month is named anywhere in the document corpus (0 hits for 2011-09 / 2017-01 / 'January 2017'; the single 'September 2011' hit is NW10+CEH2's year-long outage in the clearfell control centroid, a different matter). S.3's robustness argument - 'the interpolated-cell footprint is small', '1.3-1.6 % per cluster', 'the SSM aggregates over hundreds of monthly rows and is correspondingly robust to this footprint' - and S.1's 'match the field interpretation of one delayed monthly visit' both read as describing SCATTERED interpolation. Nearly half of it is two complete outages, and 2017-01 is a WINTER month, where the recharge signal and winter maxima live; limit=1 was justified on not spanning a DRAWDOWN season, which is a different risk. The conclusion may well survive - the point is that the current text does not let a reader see the question. EVIDENCE OWED FIRST: tools/interpolated_sensitivity.py (new, 1.0.0) runs the refit S.3 describes and never ran - scenario A canonical, B strict (any member interpolated), C breaks only (isolates the two outages), D majority - with a self-test that refuses to report unless the rebuilt centroids reproduce 03_regional_averages.csv and the baseline beta reproduce 03_03_cluster_mechanistic_coefficients.csv. NOTE doc_tier has Newborough_Methods_Supplement FROZEN (report is the only live family), so any prose addition needs ODT_EDIT_REASON naming a D-number - i.e. this wants a short D-entry, not a quiet edit. REFIT RUN 2026-09-16 (tools/interpolated_sensitivity.py 1.1.0; self-tests: centroids reproduce 03_regional_averages to 2.2e-16 m, baseline beta reproduce the committed table to 1.3e-14). RESULT GOES AGAINST THE CONCERN: masking ONLY the two breaks moves every coefficient by under ~2 % of its own value (b1 +0.25..+0.82 %, b2 -0.38..-2.11 %, b3 +0.89..+2.06 %), with b2 and b3 rank orders unchanged and every sign preserved. S.3's robustness claim HOLDS against the two breaks; no published coefficient depends on them. The move is systematic rather than noise - every b3 rises and every b2 falls when the interpolated months go, because a straight-line fill flattens delta-h and depresses the fitted drainage coefficient, so the published b3 is if anything slightly conservative. Scenario B (any member interpolated) moves far more (C2 b2 +26 %, C3 b3 -11 %, C3 R2 -0.105) but discards 13.7 % of C3's record - that is lost data, not interpolation bias, and it shows the literal reading of S.3's wording is too strict to be informative. SO THE OPEN QUESTION NARROWS to transparency, not correctness: whether S.1/S.3 should name the two months given 46.2 % of the interpolation sits in them. Martin's call; the evidence for the sentence is in NRG_interpolated_sensitivity.csv and the findings note. MARTIN RULED 2026-09-16: BOTH sentences go in, and they WAIT for the corpus pass so the Supplement is opened and version-bumped once (v2_0_1 -> v2_0_2, ODT_EDIT_REASON=D-173). Drafts are in the Fable handoff section 5.2; the S.3 sentence also retires that chapter's statement that the sensitivity has never been run, so it cannot be dropped without fixing that too.
